description:
Welcome to our project hub for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge! 

For this year's event, we are diving deep into the "Missions to the Moon and Mars" track. Operating as a streamlined, solo-driven initiative, our primary goal is to merge open-source space agency data with modern AI design workflows.
summary: Finding Space is an interactive web dashboard built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." The application documents and visualizes the historical hardware, retroreflectors, rovers, and landers left behind across lunar and Martian landscapes. By combining archival mission data with an intuitive, dark-mode card interface, Finding Space transforms technical records into engaging stories—highlighting not just what was left behind, but the living scientific legacies these artifacts continue to contribute today, such as active lunar laser ranging via the Apollo 11 retroreflector and atmospheric entry data from Martian landers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Finding Space is a lightweight, client-side interactive web dashboard that catalogues iconic NASA and space agency hardware remaining on the Moon and Mars. Users can browse through curated interactive artifact cards—including the Apollo 11 Retroreflector, Opportunity Rover ("Oppy"), Perseverance Heat Shield, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Schiaparelli EDM Lander, and Surveyor—to inspect detailed mission contexts and historical storytelling.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Space history often focuses heavily on launches and landings, frequently overlooking the physical hardware left behind after missions conclude. Finding Space bridges the gap between raw archival data and public storytelling, helping students, educators, and space enthusiasts appreciate how discarded equipment continues to advance planetary science.

Tools & Tech Stack:

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3 (custom high-contrast dark space UI with gold accents and responsive card grid)

- Logic & Data: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) dynamically rendering structured mission data from a custom artifacts.json dataset

- Hosting & Deployment: GitHub & GitHub Pages

Creativity & Design Considerations:

Designed with an immersive deep-space aesthetic, clear visual hierarchy, and zero heavy backend dependencies so the dashboard loads instantaneously across all devices.
